Making Space for Hope

For anyone who wants a little more to look forward to. Each day is one small way to notice what is going right, plan something good and keep a hopeful thought within reach, even on gray days.

Wellbeing · Resilience · Motivation · one to-do a day · you choose how many days

Start this challenge free

The first seven days

  • Day 1Name one small thing you are looking forward to later today, even something as simple as a warm shower.
  • Day 2Notice one small thing that went right this morning, like a green light or a kind hello.
  • Day 3Put one hand over your heart, take a slow breath out and tell yourself quietly, "I can go gently today."
  • Day 4Pick a hopeful word, like "soon" or "maybe," and write it on a sticky note for your bathroom mirror.
  • Day 5Send one friend a short message saying you are glad they are in your life.
  • Day 6Save one song you love to play on your way home this evening.
  • Day 7Write down one thing your body helped you do today, like getting you to the bus or letting you hear a song you love.

Further into the year

The to-dos keep changing as the year goes on. A few from later in this theme:

  • Day 30Write an encouraging note to a child in your life about something they are learning.
  • Day 60Organize a small book or toy swap with neighbors so good things find new homes.
  • Day 120Invite a friend to set a small goal with you, like a walk each weekend, and cheer each other on.
  • Day 240Say good morning warmly to the first person you see at work or school.
  • Day 365Close the day by noticing one way you helped someone feel a little more hopeful, however small.

How a challenge works

A Theraglee challenge is a theme with one small to-do for every day of a year. You choose how long yours runs, anywhere from a week to the full year, and each day you get the next to-do: something that takes a few minutes and fits inside an ordinary day. Tick it off when it is done. Nothing is scored and nothing is lost if you miss a day; the next to-do is simply waiting when you come back.

Challenges come with a free Theraglee account, which never asks for a card. Your progress stays private to you.
